author: Bobby Grayson
title: Legitimate Lean/BEAM disagreements handled by constraining the generator, not the comparison: (1) untimed timers: the model lets a stale after_run fire at any time and be ignored, the BEAM cancelled it, so 'stale i' phases are Lean-only (no BEAM action) and 'expire' is only ever the live timer, realised as a 300ms sleep with no message in between; a second expiry inside the window is unobservable (nil stays nil); (2) real time: a non-expire phase that stalls >100ms may expire the cache on the BEAM where the script did not, so a ttl mismatch after such a measured stall is retried up to 3 times (counted and printed as timing retries; 0 in all runs so far); (3) scheduling: no phase delivers to two processes, and a waiting lock client gets at most one deferred tick (a second would race its re-acquire against the next holder's release at the server); (4) dead cache: put 0 is terminal because send(Cache, ...) by registered name raises on the BEAM while the model drops sends to a dead pid; (5) run-p steps are implicit on the BEAM, so every phase is a shape with one outcome under any scheduling and the twin waits for the phase's causal end (get_state behind the message, a receive trace, a DOWN).
